name: Unjustified horizontal overflow for ordinary content
summary: Retaining full desktop width for content that does not intrinsically require a two-dimensional presentation causes avoidable horizontal and vertical navigation at constrained equivalent widths.
recurring_structure: Narrow viewport with ordinary linear text/forms laid out in fixed wide multi-column geometry, requiring sideways and downward scrolling where lossless reflow is possible.
harm_mechanism: Unnecessary two-dimensional scrolling burdens reading/task progress and can breach WCAG SC 1.4.10 where its precise test conditions and exception criteria are not met.
context: Reading forms/instructions or other linear content that can reflow without losing meaningful 2D relationships.
applicability: Two-dimensional scroll exists at an applicable reflow test viewport and the content does not require two dimensions for usage/meaning.
legitimate_contexts: A constrained subregion with justified internal horizontal navigation while surrounding prose reflows.
An implementation requiring two-dimensional layout for content meaning under the normative exception.

usability: Extra pan/scroll navigation may interrupt reading; no user experiment performed.
accessibility: Potential WCAG SC 1.4.10 failure at tested equivalent widths absent applicable exception.
maintainability: No maintainability deficit proven by overflow alone.

counterexamples.summary: Carbon explicitly documents dense full-width workflows and scrollable fixed tile regions as legitimate layout choices; essential 2D meaning requires independent determination.
counterexamples.context: Dense professional comparison or intrinsically 2D data task.

version_context: WCAG 2.2 2024; GOV.UK/Carbon/Primer docs unpinned and Carbon indexed only
